---
title: "Reading exports"
---


## The stamp in the first column

Every file [zotQDA](https://zotqda.org) writes starts with a `zotqdaFormat` column, and every row
repeats the same value — `fragments/1`, `codebook/1`, and so on. The part
before the slash says what kind of export you are holding; the number after it
says which version of the exchange format was used.

`qdapy.read()` reads that stamp and compares it against the contract file
shipped inside the package:

```python
frag = qdapy.read("zotqda-fragments.csv")
frag.attrs["qda_format"]    # 'fragments'
frag.attrs["qda_version"]   # 1
frag.attrs["qda_grain"]     # 'one row per annotation x code'
```

Four things make it stop rather than continue:

* the file has no `zotqdaFormat` column, so it is not a zotQDA export at all;
* it names a kind this package has never heard of;
* it claims a version newer than the one implemented here;
* a column the contract promises is missing.

The third one is the important one. A newer export may have renamed a column
or changed what one means, and a reader that carries on regardless produces
numbers nobody can trace. You get an error telling you to update the package
instead.

## Asking for a specific kind

In a script that must not accept the wrong file, name the kind you expect:

```python
frag = qdapy.read_fragments("export.csv")   # raises if it is a codebook
```

There is one of these for each of the exports you are likely to want:
`read_fragments`, `read_uncoded`, `read_codebook`, `read_history`,
`read_mapping`.

## Semicolons, quotes and line breaks

Whether zotQDA writes commas or semicolons depends on a setting, so both turn
up in practice and both are detected. Fields may contain quotes, the delimiter
itself, and line breaks; the reference files shipped with the package contain
all three on purpose, and the test suite checks that they come back out
unchanged.

## Trying it without Zotero

Those reference files are installed with the package:

```python
qdapy.example()                              # lists all nine
qdapy.read_fragments(qdapy.example("zotqda-fragments.csv"))
```

Every example in this documentation runs on them, so you can try the whole
package before exporting anything.

## Consensus mappings

After a code-system consensus run in zotQDA, one export says which coder code
corresponds to which consensus code. Applying it adds a column and changes
nothing else:

```python
frag = qdapy.read_fragments("zotqda-fragments.csv")
mapping = qdapy.read_mapping("zotqda-konsens-abbildung.csv")
out = qdapy.apply_mapping(frag, mapping)
out[["code", "consensusCode"]]
```

The original coding stays in `code`. This is deliberate, and it matters: if
the codings themselves were rewritten to the consensus system, every
agreement figure you computed afterwards would be inflated, because the
disagreements would have been edited out first.
